_comment: Copy to config.json (git-ignored) or ~/.config/terminal-toys/config.json. Every key is optional; anything omitted keeps the tool's default.

clocks._show_hints_comment: Whether the pomodoro key hints sit under the panel. Visible by default: the hints are how the keys are found in the first place, and starting hidden means a reader has to already know the key that reveals them. [?] toggles it live.
clocks._work_days_comment: Which days count as working days, as names (sun, mon, ...) or numbers. Drives the working-day shading.

deployments._comment: token: create one at Account Settings -> Tokens. The Vercel CLI's session is not used - it expires within hours. Keep this file chmod 600.

tailnet._comment_history: rate samples kept per peer; the chart is a window on to this

github._comment: token: a CLASSIC PAT with repo + read:org - fine-grained tokens reach only one org each, and this board spans several. The API is called directly, so the gh CLI is not needed. Keep this file chmod 600.

linear._comment: Personal API key: Linear Settings -> Security & access -> Personal API keys. Nothing needs selecting; exclude_teams is for dropping a noisy automated intake. Keep this file chmod 600.

pr._comment: Reuses github.token. Each source is one GitHub search; results are pooled and de-duplicated, because GitHub search has no OR. @mine expands to every org you belong to plus your own account.

usage._comment: Reads local agent state only - no network, no credentials. Empty agents discovers whatever this machine has; naming them instead fixes the set and the order and turns discovery off. exclude_agents drops one either way.
usage._rates_comment: OPTIONAL override. Anthropic's published list prices ship in the code, dated on screen, so Claude models are priced with no config at all. Set entries here to correct a stale price, to add a provider that publishes none (OpenAI, xAI), or to use your own negotiated rates. US$ per million tokens, keyed by model; longest matching name wins and '*' catches the rest.
usage._plan_cost_comment: What each subscription costs you per month, keyed by agent, for example claude: 200. Nothing ships here: Anthropic lists Max as 'from $100' because it varies by tier, and no invoice is on this machine. Set it and METERED adds 'the plan saves'.
usage._antigravity_remote_comment: Antigravity publishes its quota two ways: a language server that runs inside the app, and Google, which serves the same summary on the endpoint the tier already comes from. The local one is preferred and this only decides whether the remote one may be asked when the app is shut. On by default - it is the same host and the same credential the tier request already uses. Turn it off and the quota is absent whenever Antigravity is closed; the tab then says so, and names this key.
usage._grok_ping_comment: Grok is the only agent with no live quota: its figures come from the log its own CLI writes, so they move only when you use Grok on this machine. Turn grok_ping on to ask x.ai instead, using the token the CLI leaves in ~/.grok/auth.json. That also runs the Grok CLI once after a session goes quiet, which is what refreshes the token - without it the asking works until the token lapses and then silently stops. Off by default: a widget that reads should not start talking to a vendor, or starting somebody else's program, because it was launched.

link._comment: Every established connection into a port this machine listens on. Empty ports means all of them, which is the useful default. No network traffic: the numbers come from the kernel's own accounting via ss.
link._windows_comment: What w cycles the chart through, in seconds; the first is what opens. history is only a floor - retention follows the longest window on its own.

netwatch._comment: Which processes are using the network, from the kernel's per-socket byte counters via `ss -tine` plus /proc/<pid>/fd for attribution. TCP only - UDP has no counters to read, so QUIC, DNS and Tailscale's own traffic are invisible. Totals start at zero each launch.

ports._comment: What is listening on this machine. system_ports is the set hidden behind `o` - parts of the machine rather than things you started. Reads /proc only, plus `tailscale serve status` for the exposure column.
